properties.statement: Every failed or partially failed congruence-family mechanism preserves the quadratic-residue wall: its solvability relations can only eliminate quadratic non-residues, so the QR survivor classes are conserved rather than attacked.

supporting_passages.quote: Candidate failure invariant: the QR wall is preserved by every congruence method.
Blocked by the quadratic-reciprocity obstruction, not by search effort.
exceptional set is thin but infinite and protected by the QR wall
every failed family here preserves the quadratic-residue wall.

properties.preserved_distinctions: It does not merge the mechanisms: es-01 is class-local and constructive (fixed identities per residue class), es-12 is a global covering built from new solution forms explicitly designed to avoid quadratic residues, es-10 is a mixed local-to-global density aggregation, and es-08 is a meta-level obstruction analysis. They share the conserved wall, not the operator set.
properties.contrast_check: The partial-success notes (es-02, es-04, es-06) also name quadratic-residue primes as their boundary, so QR-boundedness alone does not discriminate; but only in the failed family is the wall tied to the mechanism's own congruence relations (Jacobi-symbol governed), and es-07 even dispatches QR primes within its finite range, showing non-congruence mechanisms are not confined the same way.
properties.falsification: Exhibiting a fixed-modulus polynomial identity or finite congruence covering in the notes that provably yields solutions on a quadratic-residue class would refute the claim that these mechanisms conserve the wall.

properties.statement: The failed/partially failed approaches operate in a characterizing, non-constructive posture: they classify, bound, obstruct, or re-represent the solution space without producing denominators for any survivor prime, and each note locates its stall exactly at the missing existence step.

supporting_passages.quote: an obstruction is not a solution
not a new source of existence
an existence argument the structure alone does not supply

properties.preserved_distinctions: The property does not collapse what is characterized: es-08 reasons about the space of methods (a negative meta-result), es-05 about the statistical ensemble of solution counts, es-09 about an algebraic unification of parameterizations, es-11 about constraint geometry of solution triples. These remain structurally distinct operations that happen to share the non-constructive mode.
properties.contrast_check: es-04 (partial success) is also existential ('characterizes rather than constructs'), so the posture alone is shared across outcome classes and is weaker evidence; the discriminating refinement is that in the failed notes the non-construction is itself the declared boundary, whereas es-07 and es-03 (partial successes) are constructive per instance.
properties.falsification: A passage showing one of these approaches directly producing certified (x, y, z) for a previously unsettled quadratic-residue prime would refute the property for that member.

properties.statement: The analytic/density approaches share an asymptotic-thinning structure whose guarantee weakens exactly where it matters: the bound improves 'almost all' indefinitely but is structurally incapable of driving the exceptional set to empty.

supporting_passages.quote: rare primes could in principle have none
Sharpens almost-all; does not reach all.

properties.preserved_distinctions: es-05 is probabilistic in posture (sieve averaging over a prime ensemble, polylog mean growth) while es-10 is deterministic class assembly whose payoff happens to be a density statement; the property names the shared limit shape, not a shared operator.
properties.contrast_check: es-06 (partial success) also proves lower bounds only 'for almost all primes', so almost-all coverage per se does not separate outcomes; what the two failed notes add is an internal reason the gap cannot close (polylog growth too slow; survivor classes reciprocity-protected), which es-06 does not claim about itself.
properties.falsification: A note showing the density or average bound reaching zero exceptions, or a valid inference from positive average to per-prime existence at polylog growth, would refute the property.

properties.statement: Two approaches share a compression-without-positivity structure: they unify or reorganize previously separate mechanisms into one object, and the unification preserves known solution structure while adding no new existence for the survivor classes.

supporting_passages.quote: prove that every prime admits at least one solution.
advances the organization of the problem

properties.preserved_distinctions: es-09 compresses by algebraic lift (parameterizations become slices of one variety), es-11 by constraint relations linking residue classes, es-12 by coupling solution forms to a proposed covering; the shared property is the outcome shape (organization gained, existence not gained), not the unification operator.
properties.contrast_check: es-04 and es-06 (partial successes) also reorganize ('Better organization, same wall'), so reorganization itself is outcome-neutral; the failed members are distinguished by explicitly conceding the unified object is conjectural or non-positivity-adding at the QR classes, e.g. es-12's admission it may be 'as difficult or more difficult' than the original.
properties.falsification: Evidence that one of these unifications transported an existence argument onto a survivor class it did not previously cover would refute the property for that pair.
